sections.title: A Weather Note
sections.content: A Weather Note The keeper left the lamp trimmed and wrote east wind by morning in the margin, beside a small red thread knotted twice. (Image 1) By noon, the harbor bell was a soft iron blur. Even the gulls kept to the lee side of the roof, watching a pale fox slip between the reeds as if it knew the weather first. Bring the blue coat, not the black one. Leave the white ribbon where you found it. The chart below was folded into the logbook beside a note marked harbor copy. Along the crease were nine tiny stains, almost like hurried brushmarks. (Image 2) Coal: half bin Iron: two tins Diamond: one gem Rice: a handful, untouched Thread: red, knotted twice
